samples.title: First Map: endpoint to inspected map
samples.desc: The canonical five-minute journey: connect, discover, explain, query and mount one source on MapLibre.

files.name: main.ts

samples.readme:
This is the canonical five-minute browser journey for the Honua JavaScript SDK:

connect → discover → explain → query → mount

It composes the accepted north-star journey from the SDK's public, protocol-neutral Dataset → Source → Query → Result contract and managed application kernel.

The copyable S1 workflow core lives in src/workflow.ts. In at most 120 non-comment lines it uses only published @honua/sdk-js and @honua/sdk-js/runtime entrypoints to connect, inspect, explain, execute a bounded query, and call connection.mount() with the accepted plan. GeoServices and OGC API Features use the same semantic workflow; the bounded map query requests WGS84 output for MapLibre. Ambiguous source selection, unsupported capability, authentication, overflow, and unexpected errors remain explicit states; truncated data is never mounted.

The thin presentation shell runs that workflow directly. It accepts an anonymous GeoServices FeatureServer layer or OGC API Features URL, mounts the accepted plan through MapLibre, and adds only presentation concerns: a linked table/filter, accessible popup, plan disclosure, copyable call site, runtime budgets, and deterministic teardown. It does not adapt source behavior or add a private fallback. The former standalone-quickstart and endpoint-to-map executables now redirect here rather than maintaining duplicate implementations.

The result is more than a map. The page makes endpoint provenance, source identity and attribution, observation time, authorization mode, capabilities, SDK/plan versions, accepted feature count, query fingerprint, pushdown, fidelity, cache behavior, and degradation visible. The map, table, mounted-result filter, detail panel, and popup share one presentation state without changing the accepted query plan.

Five-minute fixture run

Requirements: Node 22.12 or newer and the repository dependencies installed with npm ci. The repository pins Node 22.23.3 in .nvmrc.

npm run demo:quickstart:mock

Open the printed quickstartMockUrl. The fixture lane is deterministic and self-contained:

  • connect negotiates the configured public protocol.
  • discover inspects advertised sources and reports metadata-cache state.
  • explain creates a bounded query plan and SHA-256 fingerprint without fetching rows.
  • query executes that accepted plan through a protocol-neutral source.
  • mount gives the same accepted plan to the SDK's MapLibre renderer.

The fixture is clearly labeled Fixture replay, uses no authentication, reports committed source provenance, and does not make external network requests. The versioned fixture pack lives in samples/fixtures/first-map/v2. It contains all 48 Maui County 2025 census tracts derived without simplification from the exact SHA-256-pinned Census TIGER/Line archive. The harness binds the query limit and initial selected record to the governed fixture manifest rather than duplicating those values in UI code.

Required CI measures the path from a clean npm ci through the first usable fixture map and enforces a 300-second ceiling. The browser shell also reports narrower monotonic budgets: 10,000 ms to its first usable fixture frame, 100 ms for a synchronous filter/selection update, and 1,000 ms for managed cleanup. See the quickstart timing contract. These are machine budgets, not claims about a first-time human session or public-network latency.

Secret-free live run

npm run demo:quickstart now opens on the anonymous Maui parcels layer advertised by the demo.honua.io service directory:

https://demo.honua.io/rest/services/maui-parcels/FeatureServer/1

That public-live canary is a separate source and is not represented as Census-governed. Its endpoint-advertised attribution and observation time remain visible in the same evidence drawer.

Paste any other anonymous, CORS-enabled GeoServices FeatureServer layer or OGC API Features landing-page URL into the form. The same path can also be preconfigured for development:

samples.readme:
Load a GeoServices FeatureServer layer as GeoJSON, draw it in MapLibre GL JS, fit the map to it and open a popup on click. One HTML file, no build step, no account and no API key.

GoalBuild a map from a FeatureServer layer
LevelBeginner
TimeAbout 10 minutes
PrerequisitesA modern web browser, internet access, any static file server
Librariesmaplibre-gl@6.4.1 (ES module from jsDelivr, pinned)

Run

Serve src/ with any static web server. With Node.js 20+:

npx serve src

Open http://localhost:3000. The page reads maui-place-names/FeatureServer/6 (2,328 Maui place names) from https://demo.honua.io, draws them and fits the map. Click a point for its attributes. The <pre> under the map lists every request the page made.

What the code does

  • GET <layer>?f=json reads the layer's name, geometry type and maxRecordCount.
  • GET <layer>/query?where=…&outFields=*&outSR=4326&f=geojson pages through

the layer (resultOffset/resultRecordCount) until the server stops flagging exceededTransferLimit.

  • The FeatureCollection becomes a MapLibre geojson source with fill, line

and circle layers filtered by ["geometry-type"], so points, lines and polygons all draw.

  • fitBounds uses the features' bounding box; a click handler opens a

maplibregl.Popup with the feature's attributes.

There are no third-party basemap tiles. If the server publishes its own Protomaps archive at /api/v1/tiles/pmtiles/maui-basemap, the page adds it under the layer; otherwise it keeps a plain background and says so.

Parameters

ParameterDefaultMeaning
baseUrlhttps://demo.honua.ioHonua server to query.
servicemaui-place-namesFeatureServer service name.
layer6Layer id within the service.
where1=1Query filter.
labelFieldnameAttribute shown as the popup title; a dotted path reads a nested value.
basemap(probe)none skips the PMTiles basemap probe.

On success the page sets document.body.dataset.sampleStatus to pass, with data-feature-count, data-rendered-features and data-sample-elapsed-ms. On failure it shows FAIL: <server error message> (for example FAIL: Not Found for a missing service) and sets data-sample-status to fail.

Verification

verify/ holds the Playwright spec the sample runner executes: against a composed server with a layer seeded from the committed fixture (feature count, every polygon rendered, popup title), and against the public-live defaults. See docs/browser-verification.

samples.desc: Turn a tileset's templated link into a MapLibre vector source; Maui buildings extruded by render_height.

samples.readme:
Read a collection's OGC API Tiles tileset metadata, turn its templated tile link into a MapLibre vector source, and draw the tiles. The default is maui-buildings (about 42,000 Overture building footprints), extruded by render_height. One HTML file, no build step.

GoalBuild a map from OGC API vector tiles
LevelIntermediate
TimeAbout 10 minutes
PrerequisitesA modern web browser, internet access, any static file server
Librariesmaplibre-gl@6.4.1 (ES module from jsDelivr, pinned)

Run

Serve src/ with any static web server. With Node.js 20+:

npx serve -l 8123 src

Open http://localhost:8123. Port 8123 matters for the public demo: the cached tile routes on https://demo.honua.io send CORS headers only to https://honua.io, https://www.honua.io and http://localhost:8123. Against your own Honua server, any origin its Cors:AllowedOrigins allows works.

What the code does

  • GET /ogc/tiles/collections/<id>/tiles/WebMercatorQuad?f=json reads the

tileset: its dataType, the zoom levels in tileMatrixSetLimits, and the item link with type application/vnd.mapbox-vector-tile.

  • The link's {tileMatrix}/{tileRow}/{tileCol} template becomes MapLibre's

{z}/{y}/{x}, and requests go to baseUrl even when the server advertises another host name.

  • A vector source with that template and a fill-extrusion layer on

source-layer layer draw the buildings; height and colour come from render_height.

  • With view=extent the page fits the collection's extent from

/ogc/features/collections/<id>.

The <pre> under the map lists the metadata request, the tile template and every tile the map requested. There are no third-party basemap tiles; the server's own Protomaps archive is used only if it answers.

Parameters

ParameterDefaultMeaning
baseUrlhttps://demo.honua.ioHonua server.
collectionmaui-buildingsCollection id.
sourceLayerlayerVector tile layer name.
view-156.4729,20.8893,15.5lng,lat,zoom, or extent to fit the collection.
extrudetruefalse draws flat fills.
heightFieldrender_heightAttribute used for extrusion height (4 m when missing).
basemap(probe)none skips the PMTiles basemap probe.

On success the page sets data-sample-status="pass" with data-rendered-features, data-tile-requests and data-sample-elapsed-ms; on failure it shows FAIL: <message>.

Verification

See docs/browser-verification.

samples.title: PMTiles static basemap
samples.desc: A basemap from one .pmtiles archive on static hosting; the runtime registers pmtiles:// and reads the archive metadata.

files.name: main.ts

samples.readme:
A complete basemap backend with no Honua server — just one immutable .pmtiles archive on static hosting. The Honua runtime auto-registers the MapLibre pmtiles:// protocol on map attach, so the archive renders with no manual addProtocol wiring, and the archive metadata (bounds, min/max zoom, vector layer names) is inspected through the contract's describe() surface.

This demonstrates:

  • REQ-002 — loadMapPackage auto-registers pmtiles:// (lazy, idempotent)

and projects a pmtiles MapPackage source binding onto a MapLibre source.

  • REQ-003 — describePmtilesArchive() returns archive metadata; the PMTiles

Source is tiles-only (the query family throws HonuaCapabilityNotSupportedError).

  • NFR-001 — the pmtiles package is an optional peer, imported lazily; a

bundle that never loads a PMTiles map pays no cost.

Run it

# Dev server (Vite):
npm run demo:pmtiles-static

# Production build + static preview:
npm run demo:pmtiles-static:build
npm run demo:pmtiles-static:preview

# Typecheck:
npm run demo:pmtiles-static:typecheck

The sample archive lives in public/basemap.pmtiles (a tiny fixture; a real deployment points at any archive on object storage — S3 / R2 / GCS). Static hosts must honour HTTP Range requests, which PMTiles relies on; the bundled mock-server.mjs (used by the Playwright smoke) does.

Managed publication is intentionally separate from this direct-archive example. See the server-side contract-only managed lifecycle Walkthrough.

CDN recipe (build-less)

PMTiles works from a plain HTML page with no bundler:

<script src="https://unpkg.com/pmtiles@4/dist/pmtiles.js"></script>
<link href="https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@6/dist/maplibre-gl.css" rel="stylesheet" />
<div id="map" style="position:absolute;inset:0"></div>
<script type="module">
  import * as maplibregl from "https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@6/dist/maplibre-gl.mjs";

  const protocol = new pmtiles.Protocol();
  maplibregl.addProtocol("pmtiles", protocol.tile);
  new maplibregl.Map({
    container: "map",
    style: {
      version: 8,
      sources: { basemap: { type: "raster", url: "pmtiles://https://example.com/basemap.pmtiles" } },
      layers: [{ id: "basemap", type: "raster", source: "basemap" }],
    },
  });
</script>

With the Honua SDK bundled instead, loadMapPackage does the addProtocol step for you — see src/main.ts.

samples.title: 2.5D storytelling map
samples.desc: A pitched corridor walkthrough: compatibility gating, OGC API Features extrusions, hover and selection.

files.name: main.ts

samples.readme:
Portfolio-grade browser demo for a pitched 2.5D corridor walkthrough.

What it shows:

  • Honua compatibility gating through HonuaClient.checkCompatibility()
  • OGC API Features collections loaded through client.ogcFeatures().collection(...).items()
  • polygon extrusions on a pitched MapLibre map
  • deterministic story steps with camera transitions and an animated route replay

What it does not claim:

  • full 3D
  • terrain or mesh rendering
  • digital-twin parity

Fast Local Run

This repo ships a deterministic local review lane that mirrors the live browser calls with fixture-backed Honua endpoint shapes.

# Node.js 22.12.0+; `.nvmrc` pins Node 22.23.3
npm install
npm run demo:25d:mock

The script:

  • builds the example app
  • serves the built app locally
  • serves fixture responses for GET /api/v1/admin/capabilities
  • serves fixture OGC collections for assets, route, and stops on same-origin paths
  • overrides the basemap style to /__honua-25d__/basemap-style.json so the review lane stays self-contained

The local URL is printed as story25dMockUrl=http://127.0.0.1:PORT.

This lane depends on the demo defaulting VITE_HONUA_25D_BASE_URL to an empty string, so every SDK request stays same-origin against the fixture server. It exercises the same HonuaClient.checkCompatibility() and client.ogcFeatures().collection(...).items() codepaths as the live app without depending on a seeded Honua environment.

Live Honua Run

Point the same app at a prepared Honua environment with the documented collection names:

cp examples/storytelling-25d-map/.env.example examples/storytelling-25d-map/.env
npm run demo:25d

Supported env vars:

  • VITE_HONUA_25D_BASE_URL: Honua base URL. Leave empty only for the same-origin mock lane.
  • VITE_HONUA_25D_API_KEY: optional API key forwarded as the X-API-Key header.
  • VITE_HONUA_25D_ASSETS_COLLECTION: assets collection id. Default: story-25d-assets.
  • VITE_HONUA_25D_ROUTE_COLLECTION: route collection id. Default: story-25d-route.
  • VITE_HONUA_25D_STOPS_COLLECTION: stops collection id. Default: story-25d-stops.
  • VITE_HONUA_25D_BASEMAP_STYLE: MapLibre style URL. Default: https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty.

The app trims trailing slashes from VITE_HONUA_25D_BASE_URL before instantiating HonuaClient.

Network And Compatibility Contract

The browser runtime makes one compatibility request before it loads any story data:

  • GET /api/v1/admin/capabilities through HonuaClient.checkCompatibility()

The SDK reads the compatibility contract from data.compatibility inside that JSON response.

samples.title: Imagery and terrain journey
samples.desc: Search STAC by extent, date and cloud cover, open a COG on MapLibre and sample an elevation profile.

files.name: main.ts

samples.readme:
This MapLibre-first sample is the fixture-backed default and configured-live implementation of the Imagery and Terrain golden-journey candidate. It uses public SDK surfaces for one continuous workflow:

  • Search a STAC collection by Oʻahu extent, acquisition dates, and cloud

threshold through HonuaClient.stac().search().

  • Classify the selected STAC asset, open it through the opt-in /cog SDK

surface, disclose every bounded range request, and mount the decoded window in MapLibre.

  • Inspect asset identity, footprint, CRS, bands, resolution, nodata policy,

checksum, attribution, license, acquisition/version, cache identity, and an independent bounded bytes=0-63 TIFF-header receipt.

  • Compare the direct COG mount with supported WMS and ImageServer imagery.

The comparison slider controls direct COG opacity over the published path.

  • Query a point elevation and sample a deterministic route profile through

the public elevation helpers.

  • Enable MapLibre Terrain-RGB, hillshade, pitch, and bearing as an honest 2.5D

context view.

The sample is responsive, keyboard operable, Axe-clean, and designed to make degraded states visible. Switching assets cancels obsolete inspection and decode work, releases the previous direct COG mount, and releases the retained published preview. Disposal aborts pending work, releases both raster lifecycles, removes listeners, and tears down MapLibre.

Fidelity boundary

The offline browser lane uses the real /cog session and MapLibre mount with a lazy deterministic decoder. It proves classification, bounded range accounting, decoded-window rendering, comparison, cancellation, and cleanup; the committed bytes and decoder are fixtures, not a claim that the asset is a production GeoTIFF. The scheduled public lane separately uses the pinned GeoTIFF.js adapter to inspect a real Earth Search COG and decode a bounded window. A configured browser deployment loads that same adapter lazily for a same-origin STAC item; unsupported CRS or transport semantics fail visibly. The adapter and pinned GeoTIFF.js development dependency are sample-owned, so the SDK root and /honua entrypoints retain no decoder dependency. The pinned public asset is UTM, so the evidence does not claim browser-side reprojection or a georeferenced MapLibre mount. Scientific resampling/analysis and Cesium production support are also outside this journey's claim.

OutcomeFixture behaviorVisible action
credentialsAsset URL contains signed query values or URL userinfoRedact the receipt, refuse the fetch, and require a credential-free same-origin proxy path.
corsAsset points at another originExplain that a configured same-origin Honua proxy is required; retain WMS.
rangeServer ignores Range, returns 200, or lies with an oversized/chunked 206Cancel at the hard byte ceiling; refuse the full download; retain WMS.
crsAsset requires unsupported reprojectionExplain the CRS boundary; retain WMS.
formatAsset is not a supported GeoTIFFDisable inspection; retain WMS.

samples.readme:
A parcel viewer a small county can run on Honua instead of a Tax Parcel Viewer template. Find a parcel by its number (TMK on Maui), by street address or by clicking it on the map, and see:

  • the zoning districts that cover it, each with its share of the parcel;
  • the FEMA flood zones it touches, with FEMA's plain meaning and share, worded so the page never claims a

flood determination;

  • its assessor record link, acreage, and the fields the county data does not carry (land use, owner);
  • a link to that parcel you can copy and share.

It is a Vite app built on the published Honua JavaScript SDK (@honua/sdk-js@0.3.2, pinned in package-lock.json), running on public Maui County demo data. It is not affiliated with the County of Maui.

GoalBuild a county map app on Honua
LevelIntermediate
TimeAbout 20 minutes
PrerequisitesNode.js 22.12 or later, a modern web browser, internet access
Libraries@honua/sdk-js 0.3.2, maplibre-gl 6.4.1, pmtiles 4.5.0, @fontsource Public Sans 5.3.0 and Source Serif 4 5.3.1

Run

npm ci
npm run dev

Open the URL Vite prints. The first load shows an example parcel (TMK 2-3-4-008:053, downtown Wailuku). npm run build typechecks and writes the static app to dist/; any static file server can host it, at any path (base: "./").

What the code does

FileJob
src/data.tsconnect() discovers each FeatureServer layer with a client whose fetchFn is the request logger. QueryBuilder then runs the TMK lookup (where=tmk_txt='<9 digits>'), the point identify for a map click or a geocoded address, and the zoning and flood candidate queries, sent as POST with the parcel polygon as geometry.
src/overlap.tsConverts the Esri JSON answers to GeoJSON, groups polygons by zone_code / fld_zone, merges each group with union, clips it to the parcel with intersect and measures it with area (geodesic m²), all from @honua/sdk-js/geometry.
src/map.tsMapLibre draws the server's Protomaps basemap and the parcel outlines from the static PMTiles archive maui-parcels-static, mounted with registerPmtilesSource from @honua/sdk-js/pmtiles and the pmtiles protocol. The selected parcel is a filter on those tiles.
src/buildings.tsThe 2D/3D control uses the published SDK's scene-workspace extrusion adapter and Overture building PMTiles on the same server.
src/tmk.tsTMK input: spaces, -, : and . are stripped and only ^[0-9]{9}$ is accepted, so 2-1-5-010:077 searches 215010077. Anything else shows "Not a valid TMK" and sends no request.
src/main.tsThe results panel, its loading, empty, error and retry states, history (pushState per lookup, Back re-renders), and the share links.
src/request-log.ts"Technical details (requests this page made)" lists every FeatureServer and GeocodeServer request and every PMTiles byte-range read.

The rules the panel applies:

  • Zoning counts a district when it covers at least 1% of the parcel and at least 10 m², so digitizing slivers

along lot lines drop out. The main district is the largest. With no district: "Not in the county zoning layer".

  • Flood is a safety field, so any overlap counts. A share under 1% reads "touches the parcel edge (<1%)". With no

flood polygon the page says it found none in the county's copy of the FEMA map, and that this is not a flood determination.

  • A failed zoning or flood query says the check failed and offers a retry. It never shows the no-match text.
  • Percentages are whole numbers; "<1%" appears only when the share really is under 1%.

Parcels are drawn only from the PMTiles archive. FeatureServer answers are used for lookups, identify and the overlap math, never to draw parcels.

Address search

Address search uses the server's GeocodeServer (World locator). The page credits OpenStreetMap, so it first reads the locator's provider and only sends an address when the provider is Nominatim (OpenStreetMap). Any other provider gets "Address search is unavailable right now. Search by TMK instead." On 2026-10-28 demo.honua.io reported amazon-location, so address search on the demo stays off until its geocoder is switched to Nominatim.

  baseUrl: ".",
  locatorName: "World",

const candidates = await geocoder.forwardGeocode("Honolulu civic landmarks", {
  maxResults: 4,

"""Run and verify a 500-metre planar buffer using the installed Honua Python SDK."""

import json
import math
import os

from honua_sdk import HonuaClient

with HonuaClient(
    os.environ.get("BASE", "http://localhost:8080"),
    api_key=os.environ.get("KEY", "quickstart-admin-password"),
) as client:
    gp = client.geoprocessing()
    gp.describe("geometry.buffer")
    # POINT(0 0), EPSG:3857: coordinates and planar distances are in metres.
    job = gp.submit_inputs(
        "geometry.buffer",
        {"wkb": "AQEAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA", "srid": 3857, "distance": 500, "geodesic": False},
    )
    terminal = gp.wait(job, timeout=120, poll_interval=0.5)
    if not terminal.succeeded:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Buffer {job.job_id} failed: {terminal.message}")
    results = gp.results(job.job_id)
    feature = results["outputFeatureLayer"]["value"]
    if feature["type"] == "FeatureCollection":
        if len(feature["features"]) != 1:
            raise RuntimeError("Expected exactly one buffered point")
        feature = feature["features"][0]
    geometry = feature["geometry"]
    if geometry["type"] != "Polygon":
        raise RuntimeError("Expected a polygon buffer")
    ring = geometry["coordinates"][0]
    bounds = [min(p[0] for p in ring), min(p[1] for p in ring), max(p[0] for p in ring), max(p[1] for p in ring)]
    area = abs(sum(a[0] * b[1] - b[0] * a[1] for a, b in zip(ring, ring[1:]))) / 2
    if any(abs(a - b) > 0.001 for a, b in zip(bounds, [-500, -500, 500, 500])):
        raise RuntimeError(f"Incorrect metric buffer bounds: {bounds}")
    if not math.isclose(area, math.pi * 500**2, rel_tol=0.01):
        raise RuntimeError(f"Incorrect metric buffer area: {area}")
    print(json.dumps({"jobId": job.job_id, "status": terminal.status, "bounds": bounds, "areaSquareMetres": area, "results": results}, indent=2))

samples.title: Ask this map
samples.desc: Review a schema-grounded spatial query, approve it, then see the same returned IDs on the map and in the table.

files.name: main.ts

samples.readme:
Review a schema-grounded spatial query and execute it against six versioned incident fixtures. The map and accessible table use the same returned IDs; counts are never inferred from a SQL substring. Recorded mode accepts only the labelled exact suggestions and needs no API key. It does not understand arbitrary text. Live mode requires a separately authenticated server-side model adapter.

npm run demo:nl-map-control
npm run demo:nl-map-control:build
npm run demo:nl-map-control:typecheck

Choose “Show open incidents in this view”, review, and execute. Then group by type, select incident 1 in the table with the keyboard or on the map, and ask for those within 500 metres. The first query returns IDs 1, 2, 4 and 5 in the initial view; the distance refinement returns 1, 2 and 5. After execution, the sample is explicitly in refinement mode: the host requires every prior filter conjunct and any grouped count to survive subsequent queries. Choose Start new question to clear that context without clearing displayed results or the selected location. Moving the map also starts a new question. The (300, 400) offset is exactly 500 metres away and is included; (501, 0) is excluded.

Distance means planar EPSG:3857 projected metres, explicitly disclosed in the preview. It is not geodesic or ground distance. The existing DuckDB semantic compiler refuses geodesic mode; the sample does not approximate it with a buffer. Polygon intersection is supported by the same actual spatial engine and covered in the versioned evaluation corpus. Dates are unavailable because the fixture schema has no temporal field.

Each proposal captures source/schema/version, authorization identity, viewport, selected location, mode, and previous accepted query. Map movement, changed selection, mode, or prompt invalidates review. Refresh is explicit: propose again. Refinements preserve the previous accepted filter. Rejection, cancellation, unsupported queries and failures preserve existing map/table results. Execution consumes a review once and ignores older asynchronous results.

The reusable createAskMapSession and mountAskMapControl exports live under @honua/sdk-js/nl-map-control. They reuse createNlMapControl plans, bounded self-correction, signed approvals for effectful tools, and execution receipts. This sample admits only one read-only runWidgetQuery step. It never signs a production approval with a browser-held secret. Hosts adding effectful tools must provide their existing approval issuer/verifier and source authorization context.

The planner parses structured semantic queries against SourceSchemaV2 and compiles them using compileSemanticDuckDbQuery. DuckDB-WASM executes the actual SQL with prepared-statement parameters against a Parquet fixture whose WKB BLOB column and EPSG:3857 CRS are explicitly declared by the fixture manifest. The physical field types are checked before admission; no auto-promoted GEOMETRY column is fed to a WKB decoder. Expandable details show the dialect, opaque resource, SQL template, ordered binds and execution receipt. Grouped queries also execute the disclosed feature query with the identical predicate for map/table synchronization. Raw model SQL and approximate compiler outputs are rejected before execution. A request is bounded to 100 rows, one plan step, three model attempts, and 15 seconds total per proposal/execution. The server adapter has a 12-second provider bound and 64 KiB input/output bounds.

The engine/worker come from the npm lockfile. engine-assets.mjs reuses the existing digest-checked extension cache to self-host pinned Parquet and spatial extensions. The spatial extension is DuckDB v1.4.3 / wasm_eh, 23,469,719 bytes, SHA-256 04b776946da64a15a7b14501790c75093e38f876acc46b2922f0daeb6aaa1d60. The first build downloads missing artifacts; subsequent builds validate cached bytes. Recorded-mode browser execution uses only same-bundle assets. These optional sample assets do not enter the SDK control bundle.

samples.desc: An agent proposes spatial work; the SDK authorizes the effect with a dry run, an approval and a verifiable receipt.

files.name: main.ts

samples.readme:
This flagship demonstrates the difference between an agent proposing spatial work and the SDK authorizing an effect. The deterministic default requires no model, network, or credentials.

Run it without installing anything

Open in StackBlitz · Open in CodeSandbox

Each link boots playgrounds/ai-spatial-app-builder, a generated standalone copy of this sample's committed source that resolves @honua/sdk-js from the published package instead of this repository's src/ tree. Change the sample here and run npm run samples:playgrounds:generate.

Safety workflow

  • An untrusted deterministic proposal declares a typed @honua/sdk-js/agent-tools runWidgetQuery call and requested effect.
  • explainQuery builds an immutable query plan bound to the source locator, capabilities, schema/source versions, authorization scope, query, CRS, limits, estimates, and execution policy.
  • dryRunAgentPlan translates that plan into the shared @honua/sdk-js/agent-safety envelope and validates the exact operation-input digest, source binding, field/scope/version/data-mode policy, citation allowlist, and row/byte budget without effects. Sample-specific predicate parsing remains explicit because the shared boundary deliberately does not infer SQL fields.
  • A reviewer can inspect request/row/byte estimates, fidelity, cache behavior, provenance, and effect budgets before approving, narrowing, or rejecting. issueAgentApproval signs a single-use grant with an expiry and can narrow but never widen per-step limits. Rejection creates no grant.
  • Immediately before the first source call, verifyAgentStepAuthorization verifies the signed approval, current source context, exact operation snapshot, and an authenticated atomic consumption record. The executor consumes only the frozen authorized operation and limits returned by that function. Tampering, replay, stale context, pre-abort, or authorization drift fails before source access.
  • The complete materialized result is measured before commit. Over-returned rows, transfer-limit truncation, unexpected aggregate rows, and oversized payloads fail without rows or a success receipt. issueAgentExecutionReceipt signs the full-result digest, count, bytes, approval-use record, plan/policy/binding digests, and completion time; verifyAgentExecutionReceipt verifies both signatures and authenticated consumption before the UI reports success.

Mutation and realtime are not disguised as read-only operations. They require separate host capabilities and approvals and remain disabled in this sample policy.

Prompt text is never authority. Tool names, effects, planned operations, projected/filter/sort fields, CRS, authorization scope, row limits, and byte limits are independently checked against host policy even when a prompt attempts to relabel or bypass them.

Fixture and optional host lanes

Fixture mode replays committed parcel rows and an honest GeoServices query plan. “AI” means the proposal boundary being demonstrated; no model is called or implied. The browser creates ephemeral, in-memory fixture signer and approval-use capabilities only to exercise the shared interfaces; they are not production authority and are discarded with the session. Production hosts keep signing keys and the atomic replay store server-side.

Injected sources must supply an explicit live-host binding with a credential-free HTTPS citation, observation time, attribution, versions, and a non-empty authorization scope contained by host policy. fixture-replay is reserved for the default committed source, so arbitrary injected rows cannot inherit fixture provenance. Live-host sources must also inject a trusted execution clock whose receipt time is valid and does not pre-date observation.

Optional model and live-data integrations must be mediated by a trusted same-origin host. Provider keys, bearer tokens, signing keys, replay-store tokens, and approval credentials must never be placed in Vite variables or browser storage. The scheduled evidence runner accepts only credential-free HTTPS endpoint locations; until the external host adapter and scheduled-run authority exist, configured endpoints still produce an explicit skip without sending a request:

HONUA_AGENT_HOST_URL=https://host.example.test/proposal \
HONUA_LIVE_DATA_URL=https://host.example.test/data \
npm run demo:ai-spatial-builder:live-evidence

Without both endpoints the runner emits a structured skipped record and never substitutes fixture output while claiming live execution.

This sample demonstrates the browser-side proposal/review experience and the production SDK contract boundary. It does not place provider credentials, persistent approval authority, or model execution in the browser, and does not claim completion of the production host integration tracked in #397.

Validation

npm run demo:ai-spatial-builder:build
npm run demo:ai-spatial-builder:evidence
npm run test:playwright:ai-spatial-builder
npm test -- test/ai-spatial-app-builder.test.ts

This maintained sample is the URL-to-working-map journey for the public Honua kernel. Paste an HTTP(S) service root, select an explicit protocol hint when needed, inspect immutable discovery evidence, and execute only operations accepted by both endpoint evidence and the SDK planner.

The browser shell imports only public @honua/sdk-js, @honua/sdk-js/contract, and @honua/sdk-js/map entrypoints. It does not use the deprecated app shell, app-workspace, exploration, or client compatibility surfaces.

Workflow

  • createServiceExplorerTruthModel() validates the endpoint using the same

identity boundary as createHonua().connect(). Absolute HTTP(S) URLs are required. User-info, fragments, and identity-bearing queries are rejected; only an all-f/format=json|pjson discovery query may be removed.

  • The managed connection exposes protocol, source, schema, CRS, provenance,

cache, authorization-scope label, and capability decisions. The view shows not-reported instead of manufacturing detector confidence or schema truth.

  • projectServiceExplorerOperations() intersects inspected effective

capabilities with explainQuery(..., capabilityPolicy: "strict") and explainAutomaticSourceToMapLibre(). A disabled action retains its structured code and reason.

  • The accepted query executes unchanged through executeQueryPlan() with an

explicit cancel path and a ten-second operation deadline. Its bounded result is projected to MapLibre with projectSourceToMapLibre() and rendered as safe DOM text in the table.

  • The copy panel regenerates equivalent TypeScript from the accepted endpoint,

source, query, planner path, deadline, and cleanup lifecycle. Credentials are neither accepted as URL identity nor retained in renderer state.

The UI exposes claimed/observed/effective profile values when the kernel reports them and explicitly says not reported otherwise. It also shows conformance provenance, schema identity, CRS, pagination and authorization constraints, metadata cache state, pushdown, client residual work, fidelity, and plan cache semantics.

Truth and safety boundaries

src/truth-model.ts owns one public kernel (or borrows an injected one) and publishes explicit loading, ready, partial, ambiguous, auth, unsupported, cancelled, and error states. Renderer projections are deeply frozen and bounded across sources, fields, CRSs, extents, capability evidence, profiles, provenance, and diagnostics. Metadata is cached separately from feature data.

Opaque authorization fingerprints stay transport-only. The view receives only an exact SHA-256 scope identity, a separately validated structural label, or [configured]. Credential-shaped diagnostic and locator values are redacted. New inspections supersede and dispose stale connections, clear prior endpoint results, and prevent superseded operations from mutating the map. Manual cancellation, bounded inspection and operation deadlines, and demo disposal abort in-flight work.

The focused fixture matrix covers GeoServices Feature/Map, OGC API Features/Tiles/Maps, WFS, WMS, WMTS, STAC, and OData truth projections. If an installed public adapter cannot connect to a supplied protocol, the model returns a structured unsupported state rather than simulating discovery.

Local maintained path

The fixture server exposes a small same-origin OGC API Features service at /fixtures/ogc. It advertises core conformance, one places collection, CRS and extent metadata, and three deterministic GeoJSON point features. The app opens this endpoint by default so the entire inspect → plan → query → table → map path is runnable without credentials.

samples.readme:
This sample presents the committed, deterministic artifacts produced by the repository's honua-migrate CLI for the Honua-authored geoservices-source-app fixture. It is an evidence viewer and browser runtime proof, not a second migration engine.

The workbench:

  • loads the versioned JSON report, widget guidance, MapLibre assessment,

manifest, and patch from public/artifacts/v1;

  • imports the committed generated target, which uses the public

@honua/sdk-js/client-compat entry point;

  • compares the generated target's browser observations with every stored

expected behavior assertion;

  • retains zero-count, manual, unsupported, failed-gate, and alternative

MapLibre findings instead of filtering them out; and

  • exposes the exact fixed-argument CLI commands, SHA-256 manifest entries, and

source/target patch.

It does not accept files, upload source, read browser credentials, invoke a transform, or perform a cloud import. Artifact generation remains a repository build step owned by Slice 1:

npm run demo:migration-workbench:artifacts:check

Required follow-up step: register the widget kit

Reading a green migration report is not the end of the migration. LegendCompat and LayerListCompat carry the ArcGIS state model but render UI only after the application injects the Honua web-component kit, and the codemod does not insert that call for you (honua-io/honua-sdk-js#957). Add it once to the migrated entry point:

import { registerHonuaWidgetKit } from "@honua/sdk-js/client-compat";

registerHonuaWidgetKit(() => import("@honua/sdk-js/web-components"));

Skip it and those two widgets come up blank while every report gate stays green. The first mount in that state warns on the console and emits a widget-kit.missing event on the shim's CompatEventBus. Other container-bearing shims (SearchCompat, MeasurementCompat, …) do not delegate to the kit at all and stay state-model-only either way, so they need their own rendering plan; see widget kit registration for the full contract.

Run the workbench locally:

npm run demo:migration-workbench

npm run demo:migration-workbench:build
npm run test:playwright:migration-workbench

Set HONUA_BASE_URL, HONUA_SERVICE_ID, HONUA_LAYER_ID, and HONUA_OGC_COLLECTION_ID for your deployment. Use HONUA_API_KEY or HONUA_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN for backend-only credentials.

To exercise auth against the local fixture, start the mock with an expected key and pass the same key to the backend:

HONUA_MOCK_EXPECT_API_KEY=dev-fixture-key npm run demo:node-backend:mock
HONUA_API_KEY=dev-fixture-key npm run demo:node-backend

Control-Plane Pattern

Backend processes can use @honua/sdk-js/control-plane for hosted product administration while keeping runtime data operations on the regular SDK client:

import { HonuaClient } from "@honua/sdk-js";
import { createHonuaControlPlane } from "@honua/sdk-js/control-plane";

const client = new HonuaClient({
  baseUrl: process.env.HONUA_BASE_URL ?? "https://cloud.honua.io",
  apiKey: process.env.HONUA_API_KEY,
});
const controlPlane = createHonuaControlPlane({ client });

const maps = await controlPlane.hostedMaps.list({ workspaceId: process.env.HONUA_WORKSPACE_ID, limit: 20 });
if (!maps.supported) {
  // Deployment does not expose this admin capability.
  console.warn({ capability: maps.capability, reason: maps.reason });
} else {
  console.log(maps.value.items.map((map) => ({ id: map.id, title: map.title, packageId: map.packageId })));
}

Token and connection responses redact secret-bearing fields after creation unless a deployment explicitly returns a one-time reveal field. Do not log raw request bodies that contain upstream credentials.
